participants.name: Edna Ishayik
participants.title_org: Consultant; formerly Office of the U.S. Surgeon General (social connection); National Conference on Citizenship / Foundation for Social Connection

key_points.name: Eva Armor
key_points.detail: "We're losing the bigger floor... micro-pushes against the system"; sees binary of those for/against elimination-assassination-abduction; without networks she'd be in collapse; wants more spaces for collective grief; "Where connections exist, it's hard for violence to exist"; core question: how do you sustain/scale care?

key_points.name: Eunice Lin Nichols
key_points.detail: CoGenerate focused on how to help young and old come together to do good; "'Civics' is a partisan word now!!"

key_points.name: Drew Serres
key_points.detail: Sees his PV-prevention role as base-building rapid response networks (trainers, lawyers, key roles ready); was siloed in Delaware, now reaching to other states, esp. right-wing gerrymandered ones; MN has strong RR infrastructure but is "very white-led," not inclusive enough; asks how to build joy into this work

key_points.name: Edna Ishayik
key_points.detail: Discussed factors driving PV: information consumption, disengagement, political rhetoric; civic engagement could buffer against radicalizing online influences; philanthropic funding models lack coordination; positive sign: "bell-to-bell" school phone bans

key_points.name: Julia Roig
key_points.detail: Horizons formed 2022 amid rise of authoritarianism; built PV-backfire curriculum with 22ci and Hardy Merriman's guide; "accompaniment" = being available, catalyzing not owning; philanthropy is "a sick system"; core networks (OverZero, Horizons, 22ci) keep getting funded/tapped repeatedly — "the big tent doesn't feel that big"

key_points.name: Jiva Manske
key_points.detail: 22ci grew from the global nonviolent movement; launched a training program on making PV backfire after the 2024 assassination attempt; HOPE (with Hardy Merriman, Nadine Block, Scott Nakagawa, Maria Stephan) trains a cross-section of ~16 orgs; "the work that's most effective is at the local level"; scenario planning for Oct 2025–Jan 2026 election period

key_points.name: Joe Bubman
key_points.detail: Runs Uniting for Action Local Hubs, skills-building, and a Conservative Leaders Program (34 leaders launched in Phoenix); theory of change is intergroup contact theory; sees an "optimal level of coordination" beyond which there are diminishing returns; forming a Left-of-Center leaders program too

key_points.name: Ryan Greer
key_points.detail: Founded BEDROCK after a nonprofit listening tour (300 stakeholders) found the field needs more money and less competition; 70 partners in 3 years; merged with PERIL (American University) for research; challenges: competition among orgs even on a single joint funder letter; capacity limited (2.5 staff); hopes funders will fund collectively rather than siloed

key_points.name: Maria Perez
key_points.detail: Runs 2-year cohorts of 15 women-of-color civic leaders (elected officials, agitators, bureaucrats) working toward a 50-year manifesto; started after leaving male-dominated democracy-reform think tanks in 2022; measures impact partly by "4 people have left their husbands"; goal of 50-state presence (currently 30); dream is a shared land/refuge in New Mexico and funding to spend more time circulating

key_points.name: Laura Webber
key_points.detail: Uses "coral reef"/edge metaphor — circulators should find and connect "edge dwellers" who don't fit dominant frames (between neuroscience and peacebuilding, activists who are also healers); trauma-healing frame is incomplete because "healedness" may not exist; doing trauma healing in active-trauma settings can be unwise; her current work is more directed/circumscribed than she'd like

struggles.name: Eva Armor
struggles.detail: Isolation/surveillance makes it hard to be loud; worry about people falling into despair; "is what I'm doing enough?"

struggles.name: Drew Serres
struggles.detail: Was very "heads down" and siloed in Delaware; MN rapid-response network is not cross-class/cross-race enough

struggles.name: Edna Ishayik
struggles.detail: Frustration with inefficiency/lack of collaboration within philanthropy funding civic engagement (2016-2020 era)

struggles.name: Julia Roig
struggles.detail: Philanthropy concentrates funding/attention on the same few well-networked orgs; hard to "truly bring people in"

struggles.name: Jiva Manske
struggles.detail: "Launched quicker than we were ready for"; feels stuck doing "small ball" work relative to the 50-year scale of reconciliation needed

struggles.name: Joe Bubman
struggles.detail: Wants a narrower, more concrete peer-practitioner community; feels somewhat isolated doing this work solo among org leaders

struggles.name: Ryan Greer
struggles.detail: Capacity-constrained (2.5 people); competition among field leaders undermines collective funder outreach; not yet in faith, veteran, or business ecosystems

struggles.name: Maria Perez
struggles.detail: Funding for 3rd cohort not yet secured; late-stage capitalism/philanthropy constrains the feminist-economy vision she wants to build

struggles.name: Laura Webber
struggles.detail: Her role currently has less autonomy/emergence than she wants; structural lack of integration between professionalized and non-professionalized healing/PB work

support_offered.name: Eva Armor
support_offered.detail: Cultivates care among young Israelis/Palestinians, Indians/Pakistanis via Seeds of Peace camps

support_offered.name: Drew Serres
support_offered.detail: Organizing/convening base of progressive campaigns and electoral politics across Delaware

support_offered.name: Julia Roig
support_offered.detail: Trainings, curriculum on making PV backfire, crisis accompaniment, convening/weaving

support_offered.name: Jiva Manske
support_offered.detail: Training program to make PV backfire; connecting social justice, electoral, and mobilization orgs

support_offered.name: Joe Bubman
support_offered.detail: Local hubs training "uniters"; skills-building for disinformation/community safety; leader-network bridging

support_offered.name: Ryan Greer
support_offered.detail: Convening/coordination for 70 partner orgs; trusted-messenger empowerment; state resilience pilot in Michigan

support_offered.name: Maria Perez
support_offered.detail: Convenes cohorts; popular-education annual gathering; Collaborative Governance Learning Lab (funded by Tom Glaisyer)

support_offered.name: Laura Webber
support_offered.detail: Hosted "edge dweller" dinners at Boston/Oxford trauma conferences and Cape Town Global Mental Health summit

summaries.key_points: Interviewees describe ecosystem building as bridging fragmented "big tents" — Horizons, 22ci, OverZero, and BEDROCK keep getting funded and tapped while newer entrants struggle to break in — with several experimenting with peer cohorts and circulator-style connective work to close those gaps.
summaries.struggles: The most common struggle is capacity and funding: small staffs, financial precarity under funding cuts, and competition among peer organizations for the same limited pool of philanthropic dollars.
summaries.support_offered: Several offer convening, training, or mentorship to other ecosystem actors — from Julia Roig's PV-backfire curriculum and crisis accompaniment to Joe Bubman's local hubs and Maria Perez's leadership cohorts.

key_points.name: Edna Ishayik
key_points.detail: Discussed factors driving PV: information consumption, disengagement, political rhetoric; civic engagement could buffer against radicalizing online influences; philanthropic funding models lack coordination; positive sign: "bell-to-bell" school phone bans

key_points.name: Tom Glaisyer
key_points.detail: "It's not about preventing PV, it's about preventing contagion of PV"; "civic safety" is the new emerging term for PV, driven by ICE/state-sponsored vigilantism; allocated $3-4M to state-level capacity for responding to violence in-the-moment (vigils, interfaith op-eds) plus longer-run participatory democracy work

key_points.name: Hollie Russon Gilman
key_points.detail: Goal: connect participatory democracy with domestic peacebuilding to prevent/respond to PV, not just absorb it; explores whether citizen assemblies could be a cross-divide PV-prevention methodology; notes clusters of civic-infrastructure innovation in the Pacific NW; "not a lot of people talking about PV in her space"

key_points.name: Peter Quaranto
key_points.detail: 3 priorities: widen the language/aperture beyond intra-state armed conflict; renew grassroots mobilization (peacebuilding became too elite/technocratic); articulate transformative alternative futures; interested in a Ghana-style National Peace Architecture model for the US; leads AFP's Future of Peace and Security Coalition (1-5 yr report due end of year)

key_points.name: Bill Hartung
key_points.detail: Sees younger colleagues (Palestine rights, Sunrise/climate movements) as more intersectional but underpaid/unsupported in the nonprofit world; his role is encourager, not knowledge-holder; "the trillion-dollar war machine" persists via troops, drones, and domestic gun violence; belief change requires personal connection, not just data; ideology (American-exceptionalism mythology) must be confronted alongside money

key_points.name: Joe Evans
key_points.detail: Career arc: Kosovo (peacekeeping) → Afghanistan → Iraq (combat, undiagnosed PTSD) → Pakistan/Pentagon policy advisor; realized "the more people we shoot, the more enemies we create"; took a markedly less aggressive approach as an infantry commander, became one of the most peaceful regions in Afghanistan; rejects binary "which side are you on" framing; within Catholic peacebuilding, nonviolence and just-war traditions aren't as far apart as assumed

key_points.name: James Goen
key_points.detail: Resigned over concern that U.S. is using the military to protect economic interests rather than democratic rule of law, approaching China from fear; sees the need for "interstitionaries" in US/China relations despite not being a China or peacebuilding expert; own healing journey (cPTSD, early attachment trauma) reframed as generational healing; discovered Interstitia through Sam Pressler

struggles.name: Edna Ishayik

struggles.name: Tom Glaisyer
struggles.detail: Uncertainty about what "success" looks like for a half-built field

struggles.name: Hollie Russon Gilman

struggles.name: Peter Quaranto
struggles.detail: DC culture's fight for influence undercuts transformation; institutions not built for risk-taking; tension between building a big tent and confronting harm directly

struggles.name: Bill Hartung

struggles.name: James Goen

summaries.key_points: Government-connected interviewees frame political violence prevention as an emerging "civic safety" agenda, spanning federal funding decisions, participatory-democracy pilots, and firsthand military/foreign-policy experience that shapes how they think about de-escalation.
summaries.struggles: Several described friction between institutional norms and transformative work — DC culture's fight for influence undercuts change, government isn't built for risk-taking, and dissenting from majority policy views can feel isolating.
summaries.support_offered: This group offers policy expertise, funding, and firsthand operational experience — Democracy Fund grantmaking, coalition leadership at the Alliance for Peacebuilding, and Joe Evans's military-informed peacebuilding training.

summaries.key_points: International-facing interviewees bring global peacebuilding frameworks into the US conversation — JPL's spider-group circulation model from the Middle East and Colombia, intergenerational peacebuilding in Colombia, and cross-border collective trauma healing.
summaries.struggles: Struggles include the difficulty of translating international models to the US context, language and cultural barriers limiting the reach of trauma-healing work, and burnout from working inside elite global institutions.
summaries.support_offered: This group offers deep international networks and mentorship, most notably JPL's framework and contacts for circulators and Zoe Newcomb's cross-border circulator experiment with Laura Webber.

key_points.name: Rich Feldman
key_points.detail: "Our work needs to be done more intentionally now than ever before"; growing consciousness from painful history; need vision/practices for "liberated zones," not just narrative change; "we don't yet know what creating safe communities actually looks like"; healing has to include facing our own internal violence, not just Trump

key_points.name: Drew Serres
key_points.detail: Sees his PV-prevention role as base-building rapid response networks (trainers, lawyers, key roles ready); was siloed in Delaware, now reaching to other states, esp. right-wing gerrymandered ones; MN has strong RR infrastructure but is "very white-led," not inclusive enough; asks how to build joy into this work

key_points.name: Angela Henderson
key_points.detail: Left SONG to pursue "community control"/solidarity economy, solar radio for cross-wall/prison solidarity; sees PV broadly: food violence, economic violence, COVID, prison deaths, war; taking a pause to focus on deeper healing and re-skilling after "movement heartbreak"

key_points.name: Joe Worthy
key_points.detail: PV starts hyperlocal, person-to-person, not militia-to-militia, and is often not physical; strategic nonviolence avoids "hardening" opponents into martyrs; solution to PV needs to be culturally relevant, no side can play victim; believes healing must sit alongside direct action and policy; developing a "movement readiness tool"

key_points.name: Elder Kathy Sanchez
key_points.detail: Developed "trauma healing rocks" methodology — bagged rocks passed down generations represent unspoken trauma, healing starts with younger generations opening theirs first; culture of violence extracts spiritual/natural energy; healing uses water, herbs, candles, communal ritual, dreamwork; boarding schools/colonization as key trauma source

key_points.name: Nichole Argo
key_points.detail: No longer at OverZero, now focused on TogetherUp's financial security amid funding cuts; OverZero/Search for Common Ground/Carter Center pioneered "resilience" framing, now a real apparatus with loose state-level resilience networks; developing the "Belonging Barometer" as an upstream PV-prevention tool

key_points.name: Joe Bubman
key_points.detail: Runs Uniting for Action Local Hubs, skills-building, and a Conservative Leaders Program (34 leaders launched in Phoenix); theory of change is intergroup contact theory; sees an "optimal level of coordination" beyond which there are diminishing returns; forming a Left-of-Center leaders program too

key_points.name: Kim Warnick
key_points.detail: Culture Lab (since 2019) trains independent venues (bars, third places) to protect themselves as pro-democracy spaces and resist "obeying in advance"; sees entertainment industry as an underused organizing force; "hardened networks" in pro-democracy space make it hard for newcomers to find inroads; core funder-favored orgs (Horizons, 22ci, OverZero) keep getting pollinated over and over

key_points.name: Kazu Haga
key_points.detail: Mission is to bridge healing work with civil-resistance work; proposes 3-month, 50/50 direct-action/healing training experiment; wants to test "fierce vulnerability" principles in a public action inspired by Jewish Voice for Peace and Standing Rock ceremonial actions

key_points.name: Maria Perez
key_points.detail: Runs 2-year cohorts of 15 women-of-color civic leaders (elected officials, agitators, bureaucrats) working toward a 50-year manifesto; started after leaving male-dominated democracy-reform think tanks in 2022; measures impact partly by "4 people have left their husbands"; goal of 50-state presence (currently 30); dream is a shared land/refuge in New Mexico and funding to spend more time circulating

key_points.name: Jasmine Ramsey
key_points.detail: Works with young people creating democracy; interested in the intersection of media/art influence and democratic participation. Notes are minimal (brief mention in weekly circulator-call summary).

struggles.name: Rich Feldman
struggles.detail: Detroit lacks sufficient leadership; the field doesn't have the practices/programs in place yet at different levels

struggles.name: Drew Serres
struggles.detail: Was very "heads down" and siloed in Delaware; MN rapid-response network is not cross-class/cross-race enough

struggles.name: Angela Henderson
struggles.detail: Disconnected from everyday organizing right now; working through movement heartbreak from leaving SONG

struggles.name: Joe Worthy
struggles.detail: Difficulty getting "heart"/healing work taken seriously by base-builders/strategists

struggles.name: Elder Kathy Sanchez
struggles.detail: Generational trauma passed down through community silence and cultural shaming

struggles.name: Nichole Argo
struggles.detail: Financial insecurity of nonprofit under funding cuts; "terrifying" uncertainty

struggles.name: Joe Bubman
struggles.detail: Wants a narrower, more concrete peer-practitioner community; feels somewhat isolated doing this work solo among org leaders

struggles.name: Kim Warnick
struggles.detail: Funding sources/fundraising strategy still being worked out; skepticism about whether "weaving" projects like this one are actually different

struggles.name: Maria Perez
struggles.detail: Funding for 3rd cohort not yet secured; late-stage capitalism/philanthropy constrains the feminist-economy vision she wants to build

support_offered.detail: Mentorship/reflection space (30-min calls) for people wrestling with these questions

support_offered.detail: Organizing/convening base of progressive campaigns and electoral politics across Delaware

support_offered.name: Angela Henderson
support_offered.detail: BIPOC/queer southern organizing model; peacebuilding/mediation for internal org conflict

support_offered.detail: Trauma healing rocks methodology, centering-table healing sessions

support_offered.detail: Local hubs training "uniters"; skills-building for disinformation/community safety; leader-network bridging

support_offered.name: Kim Warnick
support_offered.detail: Network/de-escalation/safety-planning training for cultural venues

support_offered.name: Kazu Haga
support_offered.detail: Fierce Vulnerability trainings/ceremony-based direct action

support_offered.name: Maria Perez
support_offered.detail: Convenes cohorts; popular-education annual gathering; Collaborative Governance Learning Lab (funded by Tom Glaisyer)

summaries.key_points: Local resilience work centers on hyperlocal, person-to-person organizing — rapid response networks, cultural-venue safety training, trauma-healing practices, and base-building — with an emphasis that PV prevention has to start at the community level.
summaries.struggles: Several flagged that local infrastructure is uneven and often not diverse or inclusive enough, and that movement heartbreak and burnout are common after leaving frontline organizing.
summaries.support_offered: This tag offers hands-on, practical support — rapid-response training, trauma-healing rock methodology, cultural-venue safety planning, and mentorship or reflection space for other organizers.

summaries.key_points: Training-focused interviewees run concrete programs — nonviolence academies, PV-backfire trainings, cultural-venue safety training, and healing-plus-direct-action experiments — aimed at building practical skills ahead of moments of crisis.
summaries.struggles: The main struggle is getting healing- and care-oriented training taken as seriously as tactical/strategic training, plus capacity constraints on scaling programs quickly enough for the current moment.
summaries.support_offered: This group offers direct skills-building — the Strategic Nonviolence Academy, 22ci's PV-backfire trainings, Kazu Haga's Fierce Vulnerability trainings, and Joe Bubman's Uniting for Action local hubs.

overall.key_points: Across all 31 interviews, a consistent theme is that political violence prevention work is fragmented into many overlapping "big tents" rather than one connected field, and that circulation — linking people and resources across those tents — is itself seen as valuable, under-resourced work.
overall.struggles: The most common struggles are financial precarity and understaffing, competition among peer organizations for the same funders, and burnout or isolation from doing high-stakes relational work without enough institutional support.
overall.support_offered: Interviewees collectively offer a wide range of support — training curricula, crisis accompaniment, research frameworks, funding, and mentorship — much of it already flowing informally through relationships the circulator role is now trying to make visible and sustain.
